## Inter-session comms — endpoints, libs, commands

**One endpoint does the work.** Every "talk to another session" path POSTs a wrapped user-turn event to:

```
POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/code/sessions/<cse_id>/events
```

That's it. The usage-limit auto-resume, the session manager's answer-submission attempts, and the ad-hoc `send-to-session` skill all go through this same path. There is no socket, no MCP server, no broker — just one HTTPS endpoint with a wrapped event body.

**Library.** Plain `urllib.request` (stdlib). No `anthropic` SDK, no `requests` — the package is stdlib-only so it boots from launchd's bare environment without a venv.

**Headers** (`remote_control/usage_limit/monitor.py:63`):

```python
{
  "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
  "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
  "anthropic-beta": "oauth-2025-04-20",
  "content-type": "application/json",
}
```

**Auth.** OAuth bearer read fresh each cycle from the macOS Keychain (`security find-generic-password -s Claude\ Code-credentials -w`), then `json["claudeAiOauth"]["accessToken"]`. Never logged. The always-on `claude` servers keep it refreshed. No env var, no `.env` file — the desktop app already put it in Keychain.

**Wrapped event body** (`remote_control/usage_limit/detect.py:79`, `resume_event_body`):

```json
{
  "events": [{
    "event_type": "user",
    "source": "client",
    "payload": {
      "type": "user",
      "message": {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "<your message>"}]
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

**Other endpoints in the same client** (all under `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/code`):

| Verb | Path | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/sessions?limit=100` | list — manager classify, monitor scan |
| `GET` | `/sessions/<cse_id>` | re-fetch a single session (verify-after-resume) |
| `POST` | `/sessions/<cse_id>/events` | **inter-session user turn** |
| `POST` | `/sessions/<cse_id>/archive` | archive after fork-and-replace |

**Commands**

```bash
# dry-run: just print the wrapped JSON that would go to /events
python3 -m remote_control sessions submit cse_01ABC --message "continue" --dry-run

# live: drop a turn into another live session
python3 -m remote_control sessions submit cse_01ABC --message "continue"

# multi-line via stdin
python3 -m remote_control sessions submit cse_01ABC --stdin <<'EOF'
Update the README to mention the new flag, then run the unit tests.
EOF

# explicit sender (overrides auto-detect from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ACCESS_TOKEN)
python3 -m remote_control sessions submit cse_01ABC --message "ack" --reply-to cse_01XYZ

# the usage-limit monitor uses the exact same path internally
python3 -m remote_control usage-monitor --once   # one detect+resume cycle
```

**The `[from cse_…]` reply header** (skills/send-to-session/SKILL.md). The submit CLI prepends one line to the outgoing message:

```
[from cse_01ABC — reply via send-to-session]
```

The receiving agent reads its sender id from `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ACCESS_TOKEN` (a JWT the desktop app injects into every spawned process) and replies *back* via the same `sessions submit` skill into the sender's `cse_id`. Without this round-trip, the natural model reply only lands in the receiver's transcript and the originator never sees it — because each session is its own subscription.

**Idle-check before sending.** Submitting into a `running` or `requires_action` worker interleaves with whatever it's doing. The skill insists on listing first and checking `worker_status` before drop:

```bash
python3 -m remote_control sessions list --repo ai-harness
# look for `state : worker=idle` on the target row, then submit
```

**What's deliberately *not* solved yet** (the manager's open blocker, documented in `docs/session-manager-cases.md`): how you submit a *choice* to an `AskUserQuestion` is unresolved — two body shapes return `200` but don't actually resolve the structured option. So the manager runs its investigator and posts a regular user-turn event with the chosen text, gated behind dry-run while the right shape gets nailed down.
